it’s no use phrase

also it doesn’t do any good, it doesn’t help, it’s no good, it does no good, it’s no good at all, you’re wasting your time, you’re getting nowhere, nothing doing

classical

Traupman 110, 401

Īlicet.

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Other words

  • Nōn prōdest. — it doesn’t do any good

    prōsum, prōdesse, used absolutely · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 5.9.11: prōdesse aequom est, prōsum without a dative (Lewis & Short s.v. prōsum); Traupman 35: it doesn’t do any good, nōn prōdest; Traupman 23: nihil prōdest; Traupman 61

    Literally “it isn’t of use”; with the person, nihil mihi prōdest.

  • Nihil agis. — you’re getting nowhere; it’s no use (said to the person trying)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 459: nihil agis; Hor. S. 1.9.15: cupis, inquit, abīre; sed nihil agis; ūsque tenēbō (Lewis & Short)

    “You are achieving nothing” (Lewis & Short s.v. agō). Plautus also writes Nīl agis (Rud. 996).

Examples

  • Nīl agis, dare verba spērās mihi tē posse, furcifer.

    It’s no use: you think you can fool me, you rascal.Plaut. Rud. 996

See also I’m done for!.

SourcesLewis & Short: ilicet · Lewis & Short: ago

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 23, 35, 61, 110.
